notes.title: Puzzle Out VR is 33% off - permanently!
notes.content:
Since there's no more content planned at the moment, I decided to make the price for the game more attractive and lowered the price to 3.99 $ (US). This is the new default price and not a sale!

Grab a key and give it some love!

notes.title: Post-Launch Bugfixes
notes.content:
First of all, thanks everyone for supporting the game! I am really happy how the game launched! 

A new version is now on Steam. Some changes and bugfixes include:
[list]
[*] There was a problem with missing pieces especially in level 5. This has been fixed and all the content can now be enjoyed :)
[*] The minerals are not falling down anymore when the cabinet opens.
[/list]
Please continue to let me know of any issues!

notes.title: Break Crystals to Slow Down the Wall
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33779194/e0d69cda0b91bbe0f9265abc09b17cc00dae355b.jpg[/img]

A new gameplay element has arrived! Crystals can either be smashed in various ways. When smashed, they suspend the movement of the wall for 10 seconds. After suspension time, the wall continues to move at the same rate as before.

There are 3 crystals available at the beginning. They are placed in the room but can only be grabbed/smashed on start of level 2 because it’s the first wall that moves. So the crystals need to be visible at the start of the game. The cabinet is located at the back of the room so that it’s accessible anytime.

Check out the video and listen to the breaking sound!
 
https://youtu.be/8bMQ5jY3_P4

notes.title: Puzzle Out VR Released in Early Access!
notes.content:
We are so happy to announce the release of Puzzle Out VR and are excited to see you play the game!

Since we got some great feedback from the beta version, we decided to put more time into the game to make the best of its potential. The planned release date was November 2018 so with one day delay we made the game publicly available through Steam and let players participate in its development.

We hope to see you in the discussion channels here and on our discord server. We also post regularly on our Facebook page and on Twitter.

Discord: https://discord.gg/KAGWv6c
Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/puzzleoutvr/
Twitter: https://twitter.com/GlockVR

Have fun with the game and remember that we always welcome feedback and suggestions!

notes.title: Changes From First Beta Testing Round
notes.content:
The first beta testing round has finished and these are the changes:
[list]
[*]Difficulty lowered a bit
[*]Warning that room-scale is required (on Welcome-Screen)
[*]All walls move continuously now
[*]Moved the helmet UI further away
[*]Added a "Quit" button on the Gameover screen
[/list]
The changes are already live. Remember, if you want to take part in the playtesting and suggestions phase, please write me and I will send you a key that you can use instantly without waiting for the game to be released.

Thanks to Aerotactics from Reddit for providing his observations!

notes.title: Level Creation Process - Level number 5!
notes.content:
Hey guys,

Based on the latest completed level, I want to give you some insight into the process of how a level is being made in Blender. However, for time reasons, I cannot cover the whole Blender  process in detail unless there's a huge demand for it :)

First, I look for an image on the internet. I import it as a background image into Blender as a template for the 3D model:

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33779194/20a507215508caccec3f940ef8eb2315bef50a86.png[/img]

The wall is made of a quad with mesh cuts that cover exactly the borders of the puzzle image. Then I extrude each face created that way along the y-axis by 0.25 units resulting in the "holes" where the pieces are supposed to fit in. I call these holes "piece holders".

Now for each piece holder, there needs to be an object in the exact middle of it so that the game later knows where to insert the piece into:

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33779194/bb8827576eef1ddea7e4148f319e597a92eacec4.png[/img]

The complete object hierarchy for the example:

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33779194/068d6e15ffa23557006faff5ca8f1a51a9c0181e.png[/img]

The Blender file is imported into Unity where some more work is needed. Maybe I will cover that part in another post. The final result in the game looks like this:

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33779194/73794fdc3649b9b7cb933f94f5c6749b7506b0fc.png[/img]

I hope you liked this kind of post and let me know if you would like to see more of it.

Michael
